lessons.artifact: Three topics you could build a channel on, written down.
steps: Read the whole chapter, start to end.
Write down three topics you might make videos about.
lessons.title: Read Phase 0: Start From Nothing

lessons.artifact: Your topic sentence, written down, with every blank filled.
needs: The Niche Picker (Tool 01), if a blank will not fill
steps: If you can not name your kind of video yet, run the Niche Picker first.
Fill in every blank: I make [kind of video] about [topic] for [one kind of person] who wants [change].
Read it out loud. If it could fit any channel, write it again, sharper.
lessons.title: Write your niche statement

lessons.artifact: Three topics, each priced at the same view count, with the pay-per-view gap written down.
steps: Put your first topic into the Revenue Calculator. Use a view count you can defend.
Do the same for topic two and topic three. Same view count for all three.
Write down what each topic pays for one view. Keep the note where you can see it.
lessons.title: Run the money check on three niches

lessons.artifact: One kind of video you could make 100 times, saved in the Format Fit Finder.
steps: Run the Format Fit Finder on your topic sentence.
Ask yourself: could I make 100 videos like this? Answer honestly.
If the answer is no, run it again. Drop the thing that beat you.
lessons.title: Pick the format you can sustain

lessons.artifact: A 90-day target in the Planner: how many videos, one growth bet, one money bet.
steps: Write how many videos you will post in the next 90 days.
Name one growth bet: the thing most likely to bring new viewers.
Name one money bet: the thing most likely to pay you first.
lessons.title: Set the 90-day target

lessons.artifact: One idea taken all the way through on paper: subject, shape, filming day, calendar slot.
steps: Read the whole chapter, start to end.
Name your two or three main subjects. Every video you make will come from one of them.
lessons.title: Read Phase 1: The Content Engine

lessons.artifact: Twenty scored ideas in the Idea Bank.
steps: Write ideas until you have twenty. Do not judge them yet.
Score each idea against your topic sentence.
Cut any idea that fits neither what people want nor what makes you different.
lessons.title: Bank twenty ideas

lessons.artifact: Five written hooks, one for each of five ideas.
steps: Pick your five best ideas from the bank.
Write the first three seconds of each one in the Hook Builder. That first line is the hook.
Read each hook out loud. If you trip on it, write it again.
lessons.title: Write five hooks before filming anything

lessons.artifact: One filming day planned: a whole week of videos as one shot list.
steps: Pick this week's five ideas that have hooks.
Plan them as one filming day in the Batching Planner.
Write the shot list in filming order, not posting order.
lessons.title: Plan one batch day

lessons.artifact: Ninety days of posting slots on the calendar, with the gaps left visible.
steps: Lay your 90-day target over the next ninety days.
Put filming days in first. Then put posting days after them.
Leave the empty days empty. You can see them. That is the honest part of the plan.
lessons.title: Put ninety days on the calendar

lessons.artifact: The two questions asked of your last three titles and cover pictures, with the answers written down.
steps: Read the whole chapter, start to end.
Look at your last three titles and cover pictures. Ask two questions of each: would I click this? Would I keep watching?
lessons.title: Read Phase 2: YouTube Mastery

lessons.artifact: Your main kind of video, matched to five apps, with what changes for each one written down.
steps: Read the whole chapter, start to end.
Pick the one kind of video you will take to other apps first.
lessons.title: Read Phase 3: The Everywhere Engine

lessons.artifact: Posting days set in the Cadence Coach, and kept for two weeks in a row.
steps: Set your posting days in the Cadence Coach. Pick days your filming day can feed.
Post on those days for two weeks in a row.
If a week breaks, pick fewer days. Do not skip the step.
lessons.time: 20 min to set, two weeks to prove
lessons.title: Pick your posting days

lessons.artifact: One strong video remade for a second app, not just re-sent, with both results written down.
steps: Pick the posted video that did best in its first week.
Change it for a second app in the Cross-Post Optimizer: new first line, made for that app, no watermark.
Post it there. Write down how both versions did.
lessons.title: Take your best video to a second app

lessons.artifact: A clear answer on why your weakest video failed, and the fix written into the next video's plan.
steps: Pick the video that did worst. Not your favorite. Your worst.
Run it through Diagnose My Video. Find the exact place it loses people.
Write the fix into your next video's plan before you film.
lessons.title: Diagnose your weakest video

lessons.artifact: Your channel checked against the rules that will apply to you, with the date written down.
steps: Put in your channel's real numbers. YPP is the program YouTube pays creators through.
Read what YouTube will ask of you before it pays you. The date is on it.
Write down how far you are from that line.
lessons.title: Check when you can start earning

lessons.artifact: One weekly ritual for your viewers, picked and put on the calendar.
steps: Read the whole chapter, start to end.
Pick one small thing you will do again and again for the people who watch. That is your ritual.
lessons.title: Read Phase 4: Audience to Community

lessons.artifact: One video kind borrowed and reshaped for your topic, on paper, with the research kept.
steps: Read the files on the video kinds closest to your topic.
Pick one kind to borrow. Write down what you will change, and why.
lessons.title: Read the Breakout Format Intel

lessons.artifact: Your twelve numbers, each one explained with your own channel's data. No word left fuzzy.
needs: A channel with videos posted and numbers to look at
steps: Pull up your own channel's numbers in the API Explorer.
For each of the twelve numbers, write what it means using your own channel.
Pick the one number this month's work must move. Write it down.
lessons.title: Learn your twelve numbers

lessons.artifact: One real pitch, written, sent, and logged in the Outreach Center.
steps: Name one creator in your topic whose viewers are like yours.
Write the pitch in the Outreach Center: short, clear, easy to say no to.
Send it. Log it.
lessons.title: Send one pitch to another creator

lessons.artifact: Your money layers in order: ads, brand deals, paid links, products, in the order you will build them.
steps: Read the whole chapter, start to end. Then read it one more time.
Write your money layers in the order you will build them: ads, brand deals, links that pay you, things you sell.
lessons.title: Read Phase 5: The Monetization Stack

lessons.artifact: A written yes or no on merch, with your profit numbers out in the open.
steps: Read the whole chapter, start to end.
Decide for your channel today: merch, yes or no. Merch means things you sell with your name on them. Write why.
lessons.title: Read Phase 6: Merch & Brand

lessons.artifact: Your missing business papers, listed. Your channel's money kept apart from your own money, on paper.
steps: Read the whole chapter, start to end.
List the business papers your channel is missing. This chapter teaches. It is not legal or tax advice.
lessons.title: Read Phase 7: The Business

lessons.artifact: One job written down as a system, so the channel can run a week without you.
steps: Read the whole chapter, start to end.
Pick one job that only you do now. Write how a system or a helper could do it for one week.
lessons.title: Read Phase 8: Scale

lessons.artifact: Your proof of what brands pay channels like yours: topic, size, and the range.
steps: Read the whole file, start to end.
Find your topic and your size. Write down the pay range, not the biggest number.
lessons.title: Read the Rate Card intel file

lessons.artifact: A brand shortlist, worked out like a pro: found, priced, ready to pitch.
steps: Read the whole playbook, start to end.
As you read, list brands that already pay channels like yours. That list is your shortlist.
lessons.title: Read the Sponsor Playbook

lessons.artifact: The standing rules of every app you earn on, checked off one app at a time.
steps: Read the parts for every app you earn money on.
Check what you do now against each app's standing rules.
lessons.title: Read the Platform Rules Bible

lessons.artifact: Your rate card, built and ready to send as it is.
steps: Put in your real numbers, not your hopes.
Price each kind of post from the proof in step 5.5.
Read the card the way a brand would. Fix anything you would have to explain.
lessons.title: Build your rate card

lessons.artifact: The first price question priced from proof, and answered with the Kit's words.
steps: Take the first brand message that asks your price. No message yet? Practice with a made-up one that feels real.
Price it in the Deal Analyzer, from your rate card.
Answer with words from the Negotiation Kit. Do not invent a number in the reply.
lessons.title: Price the first real inquiry

lessons.artifact: Every live deal on the board, each one at its true stage.
steps: Put every live deal on the board, even the ones sitting in your inbox.
Place each deal where it truly is. No wishful thinking.
Open the Follow-Through Queue. Make it the first list you check each morning.
lessons.title: Put every deal on one board

lessons.artifact: One month of books read against the board: what landed, what is owed, what rests on one app.
needs: The Sponsor Income Ledger (Tool 20), the Receivables Register (Tool 21), the Brand Ledger (Tool 22), the Platform Ledger (Tool 23)
steps: Read the Sponsor Income Ledger next to your deal board.
Read the Receivables Register: who owes you, and since when.
Read the Brand and Platform Ledgers: what money landed, and how much depends on one app.
lessons.title: Run the books once

lessons.artifact: The hire choice, written down with its numbers, either way.
steps: Price the helper in the Hiring Cost Calculator. Full cost, not just the wage.
Price the same helper in the Empire Simulator.
Write the choice down with its numbers, whichever way you choose.
lessons.title: Price the first helper before you hire

note: The lesson spec table for the Zero-to-Career Path (Creator identity pass, rotation 22). One record per lesson, keyed to the lesson ids in assets/js/career-path.js: number and name (the manual's name formula), kind, time it takes, difficulty from the closed five-grade vocabulary (Very easy, Easy, Moderate, Difficult, Very difficult), what you need, the numbered steps, the conclusion line naming the artifact produced, and the state word from the closed vocabulary (current, superseded). Consumed by scripts/build.py (home contents, chapter spec blocks) and by assets/js/career-path-ui.js (the trail's lesson anatomy). Parity with career-path.js is pinned by tests/creator-r22.test.js.
